faq.a: Yazid is associated with the Arabic form يَزِيد, whose core sense is yazid; he increases.

faq.q: What is the origin of Yazid?
faq.a: Yazid is associated with Arabic. Yazid is Arabic يَزِيد (Yazīd), associated with the sense 'he increases'.
Yes — the underlying form يَزِيد is Arabic.
Yazid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yazid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yazīd is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Yazid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Yazid is rendered یزید and carries the sense یزید، بڑھنے والا.

faq.q: What does Yazid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Yazid is rendered یزید and carries the sense یزید، افزاینده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ya-zid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Yazid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Yazid, yazid. Script forms are يَزِيد, یزید, यज़ीद.

faq.q: Is Yazid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
